questions.prompt: In AI tools, what is a “prompt”?
options: What you write to the AI
The answer the AI gives you
A paid plan with extra tools
An AI app for your phone
questions.explanation: A prompt is what you ask or tell the AI. Say what you want, who it is for and how long. A better prompt gets a better answer.

questions.prompt: How does AI write its answers?
options: It picks from a list of ready-made answers
It predicts the next word, one by one
questions.explanation: It learned from a huge amount of text and writes the words most likely to come next. That is why it can sound right and still be wrong.

questions.prompt: When AI makes up a fact that sounds true, what is it called?
questions.explanation: AI can make up names, numbers and even laws, and still sound sure. A “deepfake” is something else: a fake photo, video or voice made with AI.

questions.prompt: What is the “knowledge cutoff” of an AI?
options: The longest answer it can write
The day the free plan ends
A filter that blocks rude words
questions.explanation: It does not know what happened after that date, like this year's prices or new laws. Use web search, or give it the new facts yourself.

questions.prompt: How is an AI “agent” different from a chatbot?
options: It does tasks, like booking a meeting
It understands photos and PDF files
questions.explanation: Chatbots can already translate, read photos and write. An agent also acts for you: it clicks, sends and books. Give it only the access it needs.

questions.prompt: You ask AI for an apartment ad but give no details. What is the risk?
questions.explanation: AI fills the gaps with guesses, like a sea view that isn't there. Give it the real facts (rooms, size, floor, price) and check the ad.

questions.prompt: You want AI to write in your company's style. What works best?
options: Ask it to be more creative
questions.explanation: AI is great at copying a style. Paste one or two of your best texts and say “write like this”. An example beats a long description.

questions.prompt: Not sure what details AI needs? Which line helps most?
options: “You are the smartest AI in the world.”
questions.explanation: The AI then asks what it needs, like the budget, area or deadline. Its answer fits your real case, not a guess.

questions.prompt: Which request usually gets the best title for an ad?
questions.explanation: AI makes ideas fast. Ask for many, pick the best one or mix two, then ask AI to improve it. You stay the one who decides.

questions.prompt: AI makes a summary of a 30-page contract. What is true?
options: It counts as a legal check
You can skip reading the contract
questions.explanation: Summaries save time, but they can leave out what matters. Read the key parts yourself: dates, prices, payments and fines.

questions.prompt: What can free AI tools do with what you type?
options: Delete it when you close the chat
Use it to train their AI
questions.explanation: Many free tools keep chats and may use them to train their AI. Keep client and company data out, and use the tool your company approved.

questions.prompt: AI quotes a law for a client. How do you check it?
options: No need, AI knows every law
questions.explanation: AI can make up laws and article numbers, and still say “Yes, I'm sure.” Another AI can be wrong too. Only the official text counts.

questions.prompt: How much audio does AI need to copy someone's voice?
questions.explanation: A short voice message can be enough. If your “boss” or a client calls and asks for money in a hurry, hang up and call back on a number you know.

questions.prompt: Why are scam emails harder to recognize today?
options: AI writes them with no mistakes
Email apps stopped checking for spam
questions.explanation: Bad spelling is no longer a warning sign. Check the sender's address, and slow down when an email asks you to pay, click or share a password.

questions.prompt: AI sorts job CVs. Why should a person still decide?
options: It can repeat unfair past choices
questions.explanation: This is called “bias”. If a company hired mostly men in the past, AI may prefer men too. People must check that AI's choices are fair.
